item.title: Database of Extracted AI System Prompts Reveals Hidden Rules for Major Chatbots
item.description:
Database of Extracted AI System Prompts Reveals Hidden Rules for Major Chatbots

A repository of extracted system prompts from prominent AI developers has documented the verbatim instructions and rules that chatbots receive before interacting with users. This collection includes prompts for models from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, xAI, Meta, and others, providing insights into the pre-configured parameters governing these systems.

🔍 Overview

The repository contains leaked and extracted system prompts that reveal the “hidden rules behind AI.” These files have been utilized by external organizations to analyze AI behavior. For example, The Washington Post built an interactive story based on these prompts, and CEPS’ AI World developed a live data dashboard using the repository’s files to illustrate the instructions chatbots receive before a user’s first message.

⚙️ Key details

The collection spans several major AI platforms and specific model variants:

  • Anthropic: Includes Claude Fable 5.1, Opus 5, Claude Science, and Claude Design. The Claude Design prompt is noted for including 53 tools, 22 skills, and 10 starter components.
  • OpenAI: Features ChatGPT GPT-6-Astra, Codex, and GPT-5.6 (Sol variant) prompts.
  • Google: Contains prompts for Gemini 3.8 Flash, 3.7 Flash, 3.1 Pro, and Antigravity.
  • xAI: Documents Grok 4.6, 4.5, and Grok Bot.
  • Specialized Tools: Includes coding-specific prompts such as Meta’s Muse Code CLI, Claude Code, and Perplexity Deep Research.

🚀 Availability

The following table summarizes recent additions to the repository of captured system prompts:

💡 Why it matters

These system prompts represent the foundation of the chat experience, establishing the identity and operational boundaries for each AI. By documenting these verbatim, the repository allows for a comparison of how different companies like Google, Anthropic, and OpenAI instruct their models to behave, handle tools, and process user requests.

item.title: Recent frontier AI model releases and API launches through late 2026
item.description:
Recent frontier AI model releases and API launches through late 2026

Several major AI model families, including OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra, Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5.1, and Google’s Gemini 3.8 Flash, have launched on public APIs. This updated timeline follows first public API availability as recorded through September 10, 2026, including details on context windows and pricing across multiple providers.

🔍 Overview

The 2025 and 2026 release timeline tracks a variety of model types, including large language models (LLMs), reasoning models, open-weights families, and image or video generators. Launch data is compiled automatically from model APIs, where public availability often precedes official marketing announcements.

⚙️ Key details

Recent releases demonstrate a shift toward million-token context windows, with specific pricing structures for both standard and batch processing.

🚀 Availability

These models are now appearing on the OpenRouter API alongside over 300 others, including releases from Hugging Face.

  • Frontier-adjacent tiers: As of late July 2026, the cheapest options in this category include OpenAI gpt-5.6-luna ($0.50/$3.00), Google gemini-3.5-flash-lite ($0.30/$2.50), and Anthropic claude-haiku-4.5 ($1.00/$5.00).
  • High-volume work: For classification tasks, the older gpt-5-nano model remains significantly more cost-effective than any 2026 release.

💡 Why it matters

The availability of these models via API provides machine-readable release data including names, kinds, and official announcement summaries. High-volume users can leverage batch pricing to reduce costs by 50% for flagship models like GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1.

item.title: State-Path Tool Menus Improve Online Agent Success on ToolBench
item.description:
State-Path Tool Menus Improve Online Agent Success on ToolBench

Researchers have introduced the State-Path Tool Menu, a framework designed to improve how online agents interact with large tool libraries by providing a short, ordered subset of tools prior to execution.

🔍 Overview

Practical agents often face libraries containing thousands of interfaces. Current constructors typically rank tools by request relevance, which may surface a final action while omitting or delaying the necessary producer tools required to create its inputs. The State-Path Tool Menu addresses this by treating the menu as an execution prior over routes from the observable request state to the desired outcome.

🧩 How it works

The framework utilizes three primary components to organize the tool menu:

  • Encoder: Represents which tools can run from the current state, how outputs satisfy later inputs, and which orders recur in training paths.
  • Retriever: Covers an executable entry, the final action, and the missing-input producers.
  • Reranker: Ensures producers are placed before consumers in the menu.

⚙️ Key details

Testing on ToolBench demonstrated the following results:

  • Success Rate: Online success increased from 0.737 to 0.898.
  • Efficiency: The State-Path menu covered more complete chains with 32 tools than the official list covered with 128.
  • Compatibility: Success gains persisted across executor families with different model capacities.
  • Performance: The system outperformed baselines involving routing, generation, reranking, and retrieval without requiring changes to the agent.

#AIagents #ToolBench #LargeLanguageModels #SoftwareEngineering

Source: The Menu Is an Execution Prior: State-Path Tool Menus for Online Agents Source: RobustSGPO: Search-Space Control for Agent Harness Evolution Source: Auto-RecSys: Harnessing Autonomous Research Agents for Industry-Scale Recommender System Source: Overview of the NLPCC 2026 Shared Task 11: Agent-Based Experiment Reproduction from Scientific Papers
